text: Mission Statement

Tencent's mission is to build a digital ecosystem that connects people, content, and services, empowering every individual and organization to benefit from the Internet and digital technologies. The company strives to enhance the quality of life through innovative products and services that are socially responsible and contribute to the sustainable development of communities worldwide.
Vision

Tencent envisions a future where technology serves as a bridge — connecting individuals to opportunities, businesses to growth, and governments to citizens. By leveraging its leadership in connectivity, entertainment, fintech, and enterprise services, Tencent aims to become the most respected Internet technology enterprise globally, fostering an inclusive digital society that benefits all stakeholders.

Tencent is one of the world's largest technology conglomerates, providing a broad suite of products and services that span social communications, digital content, fintech, enterprise services, cloud infrastructure, and artificial intelligence. Its WeChat super-app ecosystem alone touches nearly one-third of humanity.
Strategic Pillars
Connection — Building the infrastructure layer of social and enterprise connectivity across global markets.
Content — Delivering superior digital entertainment experiences across games, video, music, news, and live streaming.
Infrastructure — Operating one of the world's largest cloud platforms and AI-driven technology systems.
Fintech — Providing secure, accessible, and innovative financial services to consumers and businesses.
Sustainability — Integrating ESG principles into every facet of business strategy and operations.

text: Section 2: WeChat & Social Ecosystem
WeChat Overview

WeChat is Tencent's flagship super-app and one of the world's most influential mobile applications. Originally launched in January 2011 as a mobile messaging tool, WeChat has evolved into a comprehensive digital ecosystem that integrates social networking, messaging, payments, entertainment, information consumption, and enterprise services into a single platform.

WeChat serves as a 'super app' — a single platform that fulfills functions across communications, commerce, financial services, government services, healthcare, transportation, and entertainment. With over 1.3 billion Monthly Active Users (MAU) as of 2024, WeChat is often described as an 'operating system for daily life' in China.
Core WeChat Features
Messaging & Voice/Video Calls — Real-time text, voice, and high-definition video calling with contacts globally.
Moments — A social feed feature where users share text posts, photos, videos, and articles with friends.
Official Accounts — Platform for businesses and media to publish content; hosts millions of active accounts.
WeChat Pay — Integrated mobile payment solution enabling transfers, in-store payments, online purchases, and cross-border transactions.
Mini Programs — Lightweight apps within WeChat spanning e-commerce, food delivery, banking, healthcare, and more.
WeChat Channels — Short-video and live-streaming feature competing with Douyin and Kuaishou.
WeCom — Enterprise communication and collaboration tool connecting businesses with customers and employees.
WeChat Search — Built-in search engine indexing WeChat content, Official Accounts, and Mini Programs.

text: Section 2 (Continued): Mini Programs & Social Platforms
Mini Programs Platform

WeChat Mini Programs represent one of Tencent's most innovative platform strategies. Launched in January 2017, Mini Programs are lightweight, app-like experiences that run within the WeChat ecosystem without requiring users to download or install separate applications. They have fundamentally changed the Chinese mobile Internet landscape by democratizing access to services.

For users, Mini Programs offer instant access to services — from food delivery and ride-hailing to banking and healthcare appointments — all accessible through a QR code scan or search within WeChat. For businesses, they provide a low-cost, high-reach distribution channel leveraging WeChat's massive user base and social graph.

text: How Mini Programs Work

Mini Programs are built using HTML5 (WXML/WXSS/JavaScript) and hosted on Tencent's cloud infrastructure. They leverage WeChat's native capabilities — login authentication, payment processing, location services, and social sharing — without requiring separate integration. Tencent operates a strict review and compliance framework ensuring all Mini Programs meet regulatory requirements before going live.
QQ & Other Social Platforms
While WeChat is Tencent's primary mobile social platform, the company maintains a portfolio of other social products serving different demographics and regional markets.
QQ — The Legacy Desktop Giant

QQ (1999–present) is one of China's most iconic Internet brands and longest-running instant messaging platforms. Though its peak usage has shifted to mobile-first platforms, QQ retains a significant user base, particularly among younger demographics in China who use its file sharing, group chat, and entertainment features.

Section 3: Gaming Empire
Gaming Business Overview

Tencent Games is the world's largest gaming company by revenue, operating a vast portfolio of games across PC, mobile, and console platforms. With ownership stakes or full control of some of the most successful game studios globally, Tencent has built an unrivaled gaming empire spanning casual games, MMOs, battle royales, esports, and cloud gaming.

In 2022 and 2023, Tencent Games generated revenues exceeding RMB 170 billion (approximately USD 24-27 billion), making it the undisputed global leader in the video game industry. Its titles collectively have hundreds of millions of daily and monthly active players worldwide.
Gaming Revenue Context

Revenue from the Value-added Services (VAS) segment — primarily games — historically represented approximately 50-55% of Tencent's total revenue. In recent years, this proportion has been gradually declining as fintech and enterprise services grow, but games remain Tencent's most profitable business by operating margin.

text: Section 3 (Continued): TiMi Studios & Global Presence
TiMi Studios — The Crown Jewel of Tencent Games

TiMi Studios is Tencent's largest and most influential internal game development group. Headquartered in Shenzhen with offices in Shanghai, Chengdu, Guangzhou, Tokyo, Los Angeles, Seoul, and Singapore, TiMi employs over 10,000 game developers and has produced some of the most commercially successful games in history.

TiMi Studios is divided into three major sub-groups: TiMi Studio (Shenzhen/Guangzhou), Aurora Games (Shanghai/Chengdu), and TiMi J3 (Shanghai). Together, these groups have produced Honor of Kings (over USD 10 billion lifetime revenue), PUBG Mobile (over USD 1 billion per year), and Arena of Valor.

text: Esports & Gaming Ecosystem

Tencent has built a vertically integrated esports ecosystem encompassing tournament organization, broadcasting rights, team ownership, and platform infrastructure. The League of Legends World Championship and Valorant Champions Tour are among the most-watched esports events globally, each drawing tens of millions of concurrent viewers.
Tencent Esports — Established in 2016, the official esports division overseeing strategy, sponsorship, events, and content.
Tencent co-owns or has stakes in professional esports teams including Gen.G (Korea/Global) and FunPlus Phoenix (League of Legends, China).
Game Streaming Platforms: Tencent operates Huya (虎牙), Douyu (斗鱼), and Penguin Esports (企鹅电竞), collectively serving hundreds of millions of gaming content consumers in China.
Section 4: Fintech & Cloud
Fintech Services

Tencent's Fintech Services business has grown to become one of the company's most significant revenue contributors and strategic pillars. The business centers on WeChat Pay and TenPay, augmented by financial products from WeBank and insurance offerings through WeSure. Collectively, Tencent's fintech ecosystem serves hundreds of millions of users and millions of merchants across China and internationally.
WeChat Pay (微信支付)

WeChat Pay is Tencent's flagship mobile payment solution, deeply integrated into the WeChat super-app. It enables consumers to make in-store payments, online purchases, peer-to-peer transfers, utility bill payments, transportation payments, and cross-border transactions. WeChat Pay's QR code-based infrastructure has become ubiquitous across China, accepted at supermarkets, street vendors, public transportation, government offices, and online marketplaces.

text: TenPay (财付通)

TenPay is Tencent's online payment platform, launched in 2005 and licensed by the People's Bank of China as one of the first online payment operators in China. While WeChat Pay targets mobile-first consumers, TenPay serves the broader Tencent ecosystem including QQ Pay, online gaming payments, and B2B payment services for enterprise clients.
WeBank (微众银行)

WeBank is Tencent's Internet bank, established in December 2014 as one of China's first privately-owned, technology-driven banks. WeBank operates entirely online without physical branches, leveraging AI, cloud computing, and big data for credit assessment, risk management, and customer service.
WeBank became the world's first bank to reach 100 million customers using entirely online services, achieved in early 2020.
WeBank operates as a joint venture with other investors, with Tencent as the controlling shareholder.
Flagship products include micro-loan services (微粒贷) and digital savings accounts, serving tens of millions of customers.
WeSure (微保)

WeSure is Tencent's insurance distribution platform, operating as a joint venture with Ping An Insurance. WeSure leverages Tencent's massive user base and data capabilities to offer insurance products including term life insurance, critical illness insurance, medical insurance, accident insurance, and travel insurance. WeSure's integration with WeChat and WeChat Pay provides seamless purchase and claims experiences.
Tencent Cloud — Third Largest Globally

Tencent Cloud is Tencent's cloud computing and enterprise services division, ranking as the third-largest cloud service provider globally by infrastructure scale and market share. Tencent Cloud provides a comprehensive suite of cloud services including computing, storage, databases, networking, security, AI, and big data analytics — serving millions of businesses, governments, and developers worldwide.

Tencent Cloud operates in over 60 availability zones across 26 geographic regions globally, serving clients in finance, gaming, education, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, and government sectors. Its infrastructure is deeply integrated with Tencent's AI capabilities, enabling enterprise clients to deploy AI-powered applications rapidly.

text: Section 4 (Continued): Enterprise Services
Enterprise Services Overview

Tencent's enterprise services encompass a broad range of business productivity tools, communication platforms, and industry-specific solutions. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated enterprise digitalization in China, and Tencent has been a primary beneficiary through its suite of cloud-based enterprise tools.
Tencent Meeting (腾讯会议)

Tencent Meeting is an enterprise-grade video conferencing platform launched in December 2019. It quickly became one of China's most popular video conferencing tools, supporting HD video meetings, screen sharing, virtual backgrounds, cloud recording, and meeting scheduling. During COVID-19, Tencent Meeting experienced exponential growth, reaching over 100 million registered users within months of launch.
Available on Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, and via web browser, with enterprise versions offering administrative controls, SSO integration, and analytics dashboards.
Tencent Meeting Rooms is an enterprise hardware solution for conference room deployment, including dedicated roomkits.
WeCom (企业微信)

WeCom is Tencent's enterprise communication and customer relationship management (CRM) tool. WeCom serves as a comprehensive business communication platform that enables companies to connect with customers via WeChat, manage employee communications, and integrate third-party business applications.

WeCom allows businesses to create official WeChat accounts that communicate with customers through the WeChat interface — enabling businesses to leverage WeChat's 1.3B+ user base for customer service, marketing, and sales.
WeCom supports workflow automation, approval systems, attendance tracking (考勤打卡), expense reporting, and ERP integrations.
Tencent Security (腾讯安全)

Tencent Security provides a comprehensive suite of cybersecurity products and services protecting Tencent's own platforms as well as enterprise clients. Offerings include DDoS protection, web application firewall (WAF), vulnerability assessment, threat intelligence, and cloud security services.
Tencent Security collaborates with government agencies and international organizations on cybersecurity research and incident response.
The T-Sec portfolio includes endpoint detection and response (EDR), security operation center (SOC) services, and compliance assessment tools.
Section 5: AI & Innovation
AI Strategy Overview

Tencent has positioned artificial intelligence as a core strategic pillar, investing heavily in AI research, development, and deployment across all business units. The company's AI strategy encompasses proprietary foundation models, applied AI in healthcare, entertainment, and enterprise services, as well as fundamental research conducted through its network of AI laboratories.

Tencent's AI investments span the full value chain — from fundamental research (Tencent AI Lab, Robotics X) to applied research (Tencent Healthcare AI, Tencent Security AI) to product integration (Hunyuan in WeChat, Tencent Cloud AI, gaming AI). In September 2023, Tencent launched Hunyuan, its proprietary large-scale AI foundation model, marking a significant milestone in the company's AI journey.
Tencent AI Lab

The Tencent AI Lab (人工智能实验室) was established in 2016 as Tencent's primary research arm for artificial intelligence. Based primarily in Shenzhen with research staff in Seattle and other international locations, the AI Lab focuses on machine learning, computer vision, speech recognition, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. The Lab's research has been published in top-tier academic conferences including NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, and ACL.
The AI Lab has developed AlphaSense, a game-playing AI that has achieved professional-level performance in multiple games including StarCraft II and Honor of Kings.
The Lab's research into Large Language Models (LLMs) contributed to the development of Tencent Hunyuan.
AI Lab's speech synthesis technology powers Tencent's smart speaker products and voice interaction features across WeChat and QQ.
Tencent Hunyuan Foundation Model

Tencent Hunyuan (腾讯混元) is Tencent's proprietary large-scale AI foundation model, officially launched in September 2023. Hunyuan is a pre-trained generative model capable of a wide range of natural language tasks including text generation, summarization, translation, question answering, and code completion. It has been integrated across Tencent's product ecosystem, including WeChat Search, Tencent Meeting, Tencent Cloud, and enterprise services.

text: Healthcare AI — Tencent MedTec

Tencent MedTec (腾讯医疗) applies AI to healthcare challenges, including medical imaging analysis, drug discovery, and health monitoring. Tencent's AI-driven medical imaging technology has been deployed in hospitals across China, assisting radiologists in detecting early-stage cancers and other conditions. The company also operates AI-powered health management platforms integrated with WeChat.
Tencent's AI for medical imaging has received regulatory approval as a Class III medical device in China.
The company has partnerships with leading Chinese hospitals including Peking Union Medical College Hospital and Ruijin Hospital.
Tencent's AI-driven drug discovery platform leverages machine learning to accelerate the identification of drug candidates.
Technology Infrastructure

Tencent operates one of the world's largest technology infrastructures, comprising massive data centers across China and internationally, a proprietary content delivery network (CDN), and advanced AI computing clusters. The infrastructure supports over 1.3 billion WeChat users, the world's largest gaming platform, a leading cloud business, and an AI research operation.
Computing Infrastructure
Tencent operates over 100 data centers globally, including major facilities in Shenzhen, Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou, Chengdu, and multiple international locations.
The company's AI computing clusters use NVIDIA and other advanced GPU accelerators to train large-scale AI models including Hunyuan.
Tencent's proprietary network infrastructure handles over 10 petabytes of data traffic daily across its platforms.
The company has made significant investments in custom AI accelerators and heterogeneous computing to optimize training and inference costs.
Research & Development

Tencent's commitment to R&D is reflected in its substantial annual research spending and its network of dedicated research institutes. The company invests over RMB 60 billion annually in R&D, with a significant portion allocated to AI, cloud computing, and emerging technologies.

Section 7: Financial Performance
Revenue Breakdown by Segment

Tencent's revenue is organized into three primary reporting segments: (1) Value-added Services (VAS), (2) FinTech and Business Services, and (3) Online Advertising. Within VAS, the two key sub-segments are Social Networks and Games. The FinTech and Business Services segment encompasses WeChat Pay, TenPay, cloud services, and other enterprise offerings.

In FY2023, Tencent reported total revenue of approximately RMB 554.6 billion (approximately USD 79 billion), representing a return to growth after a challenging 2022. Net profit attributable to equity holders was approximately RMB 115.2 billion (approximately USD 16 billion), reflecting strong operating leverage as the company benefited from cost optimization initiatives.

text: Section 8: ESG & Sustainability
ESG Strategy & Framework

Tencent has significantly strengthened its Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework in recent years, publishing comprehensive ESG reports aligned with global standards including the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), and the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The company has established dedicated ESG committees at the board level and integrated sustainability metrics into executive compensation.

In 2023, Tencent received an ESG rating of 'A' from MSCI (Morgan Stanley Capital International) and was included in the Hang Seng ESG 50 Index. The company has committed to achieving carbon neutrality in its own operations (Scope 1 and 2) by 2030 and has set Science-Based Targets for Scope 3 emissions reduction.
Governance

Tencent operates under a dual-class share structure that concentrates voting control with the founding team (primarily Pony Ma and co-founders), ensuring long-term strategic stability. The Board of Directors includes a mix of executive directors, independent non-executive directors, and directors with expertise in technology, finance, law, and international business.
The Board has established dedicated committees: Audit Committee, Remuneration Committee, and Corporate Governance Committee, all with independent non-executive director chairs.
Tencent has implemented robust anti-corruption policies, data privacy frameworks, and cybersecurity governance practices compliant with Chinese and international standards.
The company publishes an annual ESG report, tax contribution report, and carbon emission disclosure aligned with TCFD recommendations.
Green Technology & Carbon Neutrality Goals

Tencent has committed to achieving carbon neutrality in its own operations (Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions) by 2030. The company is also working with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) to set long-term Scope 3 emission reduction targets for its value chain.

text: Green Technology Initiatives
Tencent Cloud's QingTian AI Computing Cluster uses advanced liquid cooling technology to reduce energy consumption by up to 40% compared to traditional air-cooled data centers.
The company has deployed over 100 MW of solar capacity at its data center campuses in China.
Tencent's Green Server Program extends hardware lifecycle, reducing e-waste and the environmental impact of frequent server replacements.
The company uses AI optimization for data center cooling, reducing Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) to as low as 1.2 at newer facilities.
Social Responsibility Programs

Tencent has built an extensive social responsibility program that leverages its technology and resources to address societal challenges. The company focuses on digital inclusion, education, healthcare, poverty alleviation, and cultural preservation.
Key Social Initiatives

Tencent Philanthropy Foundation (腾讯公益慈善基金会) — One of China's largest corporate philanthropies, focusing on rural education, healthcare, and poverty alleviation. The foundation has donated billions of RMB over the years.
WeChat Health (微信医保) — Integrates medical appointment booking, health insurance, and medical record access through WeChat, improving healthcare access in underserved regions.
Rural Digitalization Program — Leverages Mini Programs and WeChat to provide digital tools for rural entrepreneurs, farmers, and small businesses, helping bridge the urban-rural digital divide.

Tencent Games' Social Impact — Gaming titles are used for educational purposes, including language learning, cultural preservation (e.g., Li Bai poetry in Honor of Kings), and mental health awareness campaigns.

Digital Heritage — Tencent supports the preservation of Chinese cultural heritage through technology, including digital archiving of cultural artifacts and heritage site monitoring using cloud and AI technologies.

COVID-19 Response — During the pandemic, Tencent contributed over RMB 1.5 billion in financial and in-kind donations, deployed Health Code technology, and provided free cloud computing resources for medical research.
